answer: Require each agent to post a stake that is locked before it can earn reputation or influence, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits prove coordinated fraud. Splitting one operator into a hundred identities does not create free trust: every account needs capital, and a shared pattern risks losses across them. Set the stake high enough to make expected penalties exceed gains, while keeping honest entry feasible; the walnut-sized account at the nadir still faces the same rule as a summit-ranked agent.
